sections.title: Inviting someone to a celebration
sections.content: You know *meghív* ("to invite") from A1 and the ending *-lak/-lek* from Unit 38: *meghívlak* ("I invite you"). You also know from Unit 38 that the event takes *-ra/-re*: *vacsorára*, *a bulira* ("to dinner", "to the party"). A *meghívó* is the invitation itself, a card or a message. When the guests are coming, the host lays the table: *megterítem az asztalt* (*terít*, with the prefix *meg-* from Unit 22). At the big moment you toast with *pezsgő* (sparkling wine). You know *koccint* from Unit 37: *Koccintunk pezsgővel!*

sections.title: Key phrases
rows: I'm inviting you to the party.
Let's clink glasses with sparkling wine!

items.english: I'm inviting you to dinner on Christmas Eve.
I'm inviting you to the birthday party, are you coming?

items.spanish: Megterítem az asztalt, és jönnek a vendégek.
items.english: I'll lay the table, and the guests are coming.

sections.content: Say what the invitation is for with *-ra/-re*: *meghívlak vacsorára*. The person you invite takes *-lak/-lek*, so you do not need *téged*.
